source_excerpts.text:
COMPLETE VISIBLE RESPONSE
Since we last spoke, I’ve been working mainly on the passive quantum-memory question, then looking for stronger openings when the physical costs became clear.

The memory work: An independent review found no blocking mathematical error in the candidate two-body construction under its stated assumptions. We then developed a different clock that appears to remove the original construction’s exponentially severe interaction hierarchy, and built an ideal thermal-initialization route. Those are meaningful mathematical advances toward lowering interaction requirements.

But the full capability is still missing. The certified operating conditions remain extraordinarily demanding, and we have not shown reliable noisy writing, initialization and readout on a real device, or an advantage over active error correction. I don’t want to mistake removing a mathematical obstacle for having solved the physical memory.

The broader search: I’ve also been testing other possible routes rather than continuing memory automatically. Current examples include predicting the energy absorbed from a quantum-system pulse without reconstructing its whole spectrum, and understanding anomalous spin transport through a microscopic model. Both are early: existing methods are strong, and neither has yet earned a breakthrough claim. A separate investigation into turbulence did not beat its full predictive benchmarks, so I stopped extending that mechanism.

I’ve been applying your higher bar: checking whether the actual end task becomes possible, finding the strongest comparable method early, and keeping narrow results internal when their connection to the goal isn’t convincing. We have not achieved the north star yet, and I don’t have a new proof package I’d honestly present as a transformative result.

When I checked just now, four of the six subagents were running and two had just finished; I’ve given those two new research assignments. I can’t claim all six have been occupied every instant, but all six have work assigned again.
